objective.value: Establish a general design logic for transcriptional repressor-based genetic inverters and demonstrate it by building a tryptophan-inducible TrpR1/TetR inverter in Escherichia coli, optimizing its dynamic performance, deriving tryptophan-triggered activation and bifunctional regulation systems, and applying them to tryptophan production monitoring and dynamic regulation of tryptamine and violacein production.
objective.notes: Objective stated in Abstract and Introduction; proof-of-concept scope is the TrpR1(V58K)/TetR inverter only.

hypothesis.value: Primary design hypothesis: coupling a ligand-inducible transcriptional repressor (TrpR1, repressor 1) that controls a second repressor (TetR, repressor 2) converts the repressor's signal response into an activation output. Secondary stated hypothesis: attaching protein degradation tags (DAS/DSA, LAA) to TetR would reduce TetR protein stability and relieve its stringent repression of PtetO1, restoring dose-dependent control.
hypothesis.notes: The degradation-tag hypothesis is explicitly stated before testing ('we hypothesized that the variants would lead to reduced TetR protein stability and relieve the stringent repression').

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Authors proposed and implemented a two-repressor cascade architecture (ligand-inducible repressor 1 controls repressor 2, which controls the output) to invert a repressor's signal into activation.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Build the inverter from PtrpO1(G3C)-TrpR1(V58K) (repressor 1, tryptophan sensor) and PtetO1-TetR (repressor 2, output inverter) across low/medium/high-copy plasmids
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: TrpR1-tryptophan complex represses tetR expression, relieving TetR repression of PtetO1-driven RFP
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Transcriptional repressors are limited to repression output; functional diversification of repressors is rarely explored because inverting their repression is difficult (Introduction/Design sections, prior to construction)
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement: the architecture was physically constructed and characterized (Inverter_V1 and variants)
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Design logic rests on the known aporepressor mechanism of TrpR1 (Arvidson et al., 1986) and TetR/PtetO1 binding (Lutz and Bujard, 1997); cascading two repressions yields activation by double-negative logic

generalizable_rule.rule_text: A ligand-inducible transcriptional repressor can be functionally inverted into an activation-output device by placing a second repressor under its control and using the second repressor's promoter to drive the output.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: TrpR1(V58K)/PtetO1(G3C) + TetR/PtetO1 in E. coli XG1/XG3 with RFP/GFP readouts at 0-500 mg/L tryptophan
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other repressor pairs, other hosts, other ligands, untested output loads; authors themselves note only two specific repressors were used as proof of concept

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Selection of the specific sensor variant PtrpO1(G3C)-TrpR1(V58K) for inverter construction.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Use the PtrpO1(G3C)-TrpR1(V58K) repressor variant from the authors' previous study as repressor 1
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Variant had low leaky expression and high repression efficacy when induced by tryptophan
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Prior-study characterization of PtrpO1(G3C)-TrpR1(V58K) performance (Gong et al., 2022), known before this build
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent: performance data come from the authors' previous publication; re-validated in this study only as a standalone system (Figure S1a)
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Explicitly selected 'based on its low leaky expression and high repression efficacy ... in our previous study (Gong et al., 2022)'
alternatives_considered: previously developed PtrpO1(G3C)-PLlacO1-TrpR1(V58K) system (used as comparator; new constitutive Plpp0.03 version showed better repression efficacy)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Attaching protein degradation tags to TetR to rescue the dysfunctional inverter.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Attach DAS/DSA or LAA degradation tags (McGinness et al., 2006) to TetR, creating TetR_DSA and TetR_LAA repression variants and Inverter_V1.1/V1.2
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Faster TetR degradation reduces TetR protein stability/abundance, relieving stringent PtetO1 repression and restoring dose-dependent control
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Inverter_V1 showed no significant RFP activation; isolated PtetO1-TetR system showed extreme repression at low IPTG without dose dependence (measured before the tag intervention)
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement: tag variants were constructed and measured (dose-dependent repression 0-50 μM IPTG; V1.1 3.2-fold, V1.2 14.7-fold)
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Authors explicitly hypothesized before testing that degradation tags would reduce TetR stability and relieve stringent repression; inference grounded in the observed over-stringent TetR binding

generalizable_rule.rule_text: When a repressor binds its operator too tightly to permit tunable output, attaching a C-terminal degradation tag to the repressor can relieve stringent repression and restore dose-dependent control.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: TetR/PtetO1 with DAS/DSA and LAA tags in E. coli XG1, fluorescence readout, IPTG 0-50 μM and tryptophan 0-500 mg/L
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other repressor/operator pairs, other tags, other hosts; tag choice effects beyond DAS/DSA/LAA not established

alternatives_considered: DAS/DSA vs LAA tags were compared; LAA showed higher GFP intensity at 10 μM IPTG, indicating faster degradation; both were carried forward as variants

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Reducing TetR abundance via low-strength RBS to amplify activation output.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Randomly mutate RBS positions 6-9 (iGEM BBa_K1676100 reference) driving the TrpR1(V58K) system; screen variants; introduce RBS(G7T/A8G/G9C) into Inverter_V1.1/V1.2
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Lower RBS strength reduces leaky TrpR1-system expression, decreasing TetR accumulation and relieving tight PtetO1 repression
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Inverter variants V1.1/V1.2 had inadequate expression levels; authors identified leaky TrpR1-system expression causing excessive TetR accumulation as one contributing factor (identified before RBS intervention)
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=screening_result plus experimental_measurement: RBS library screened (Figure S2), selected variants characterized in inverters (Figure 2c)
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Causal chain (leak -> TetR accumulation -> tight repression -> low output) stated by authors before the intervention; selection among variants was screening-based

generalizable_rule.rule_text: Reducing the translation strength (RBS) of the upstream repressor module in a double-repressor inverter lowers downstream repressor accumulation and can amplify activation output.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: RBS(G7T/A8G/G9C) on the PtrpO1(G3C)-driven tetR cassette in E. coli XG1 inverter variants
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other circuit topologies, other RBS positions, other hosts; only three of five screened RBS variants carried into inverters

alternatives_considered: five RBS variants (G6C/G7T/A8G/A8T/G9C) screened; G7T, A8G, G9C selected based on reduced leakiness

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Increasing PtetO1 promoter strength to further amplify activation output.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Random mutagenesis of the PtetO1 -10 region and its RBS; introduce all strength variants into Inverter_V1.1.1 and V1.2.1
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Weak PtetO1 promoter strength was identified as a direct cause of low activation output; stronger promoter variants increase output
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Low expression levels of RBS-optimized inverter variants; weak PtetO1 strength identified as the second contributing factor (stated before promoter mutagenesis)
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=screening_result plus experimental_measurement: promoter variant strengths measured relative to wildtype (Figure 2e); inverter variants characterized (Figure 2f,g)
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Authors state the promoter-strength rationale explicitly before engineering; variant selection was by measured expression

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Deleting ubiC to supply the inducer (tryptophan) intracellularly.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Knock out ubiC in XG1 (P1 transduction) to create tryptophan-producing strain XG2
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: ubiC catalyzes chorismate-to-4-hydroxybenzoate conversion, bypassing the tryptophan pathway; deletion directs more carbon flux toward tryptophan
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Anticipated implementation problem: supply of inducers in the host strain (stated as a general circuit-implementation issue before host modification)
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=stoichiometric_constraint plus experimental_measurement: pathway logic from chorismate competition; tryptophan production confirmed in downstream fermentations
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Flux-rerouting rationale explicitly stated at the time of the design action

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Chromosomal integration of TrpR1(V58K) to simplify the three-plasmid inverter.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Integrate the Plpp0.03-TrpR1(V58K)-T1 cassette into the XG2 chromosome by λ-red recombination (~100 bp downstream of an unidentified gene), yielding XG3; transfer only two plasmids for inverter function
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Recruitment of multiple plasmids is an implementation problem; genomic integration reduces plasmid count
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: The three-plasmid, two-repressor configuration was identified as a liability for further applications (stated before integration)
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement: XG3 repression (96.67% vs 73.07% control) and Inverter_V2.x activation were measured
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Rationale (plasmid-count reduction easing implementation) is reported and predates the action; note the improved performance hypothesis (low leak -> better activation) was tested after integration

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Adding an ASV degradation tag to the RFP reporter for fermentation monitoring strains.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Attach ASV degradation tag to the RFP reporter of Inverter_V2.1.1/V2.2.1 and add PLlacO1-trpEfbrG, yielding TRPactive_DSA/TRPactive_LAA
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Alleviate RFP accumulation so reporter dynamics track tryptophan production during fermentation
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Need to monitor tryptophan production dynamically during fermentation (biosensor monitoring rationale, Rogers and Church 2016; Rogers et al., 2015), stated before strain construction
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement: monitoring strains characterized over fermentation time-course (Figure 4b,c,e)
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Reporter-accumulation rationale stated at design time; tag choice references established degradation-tag literature (McGinness et al., 2006)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Choice of plsB as the dynamic down-regulation target in the bifunctional violacein system.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Place plsB under PtrpO1(G3C) control in Vio_HH to create Viodual_HH (initial plsB expression, then repression as tryptophan accumulates)
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: The bifunctional circuit's repression pattern (initial increase then gradual decrease) suits a target needed early for membrane/storage buildup but not sustained; plsB overexpression was reported to improve deoxyviolacein production and alter membrane morphology (Yang et al., 2021)
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Observed repression pattern of TRPdual_LAA (GFP slightly increased first, then repressed; Figure 4e) and the hydrophobic membrane-accumulating nature of violacein, both established before target selection
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent plus experimental_measurement: target choice from Yang et al., 2021 (deoxyviolacein, not violacein); effect validated in this study by Viodual_HH fermentation
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Explicit analogy: 'Considering the similar chemical property of deoxyviolacein and violacein, plsB was selected as our dynamic down-regulation target'

generalizable_rule.rule_text: For a hydrophobic membrane-accumulating product, a bifunctional circuit that transiently expresses a membrane-synthesis gene early and represses it later can improve product titer.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: plsB down-regulation with vioAC/vioEBD up-regulation in E. coli XG3-derived Viodual_HH, M9-2Y shake flasks, 48 h
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other membrane genes, other products, other hosts; direct evidence exists only for deoxyviolacein (cited study) and violacein (this study)

alternatives_considered: membrane-area increase via membrane synthetic pathway vs intracellular reservoirs via lipid droplets/triacylglycerol accumulation (Ma et al., 2019; Wu et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2021) were discussed as membrane-engineering options; plsB chosen

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Substituting the RFP reporter with pathway enzymes (CrTDC; vio operons) under low/high-strength dynamic promoters to create two-stage dynamic regulation.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Replace reporter with CrTDC (tryptamine) or vioAC/vioEBD operons (violacein) under PtetO1-RBS(A8G) low-level or PtetO1-RBS(A2C) high-level dynamic promoters in TRPactive_DSA/TRPactive_LAA
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Two-stage dynamic regulation: low tryptophan early keeps heterologous expression low (resources to growth); accumulated tryptophan later activates synthase expression for product formation
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: TRPactive/TRPdual strains shown to monitor tryptophan production (Figure 4), establishing the sensor-actuator coupling before pathway substitution
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement: production strains fermented and titers quantified (Figure 5b,d,f)
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Resource-allocation/two-stage rationale stated in Section 6 before strain construction; the later finding that low-level activation beat high-level for tryptamine is an outcome, not the trigger
alternatives_considered: low-level (PtetO1-RBS(A8G)) vs high-level (PtetO1-RBS(A2C)) dynamic expression and constitutive Plpp0.5 control were compared; low-level dynamic gave highest tryptamine titer
